q: 1. The process at which steel is passed through a small hole to make cylindrical rods and wires is:
explain: Drawing is the process of pulling steel through a die (small hole) to produce thin cylindrical rods and wires.

q: 2. A prime coat is given to steel work
options: a mixture of linseed oil & red lead
explain: The standard primer for steel is red lead mixed with linseed oil to prevent oxidation.

q: 3. Aluminium is extensively used in aeroplane industries because
options: its tensile strength is very low
it is very tough and light metal
explain: Aluminum's high strength-to-weight ratio (tough but lightweight) makes it the primary material for aircraft construction.

q: 4. The crudest form of iron is
explain: Cast iron (or Pig iron directly from the furnace) is the crudest form, containing high carbon content and impurities.

q: 5. The process at which steel is passed through a small hole to make cylindrical rods and wires is
explain: as per key c but Drawing is the manufacturing process used to reduce the cross-section of a wire or rod by pulling it through a die.

q: 6. Addition of chromium to steel makes it
explain: Chromium increases the corrosion resistance and can enhance the elasticity and hardness of steel.

q: 7. Major component of a gun metal is
explain: Gunmetal is a type of bronze primarily composed of Copper (88%), with Tin and Zinc.
